Forecast Discussion

A cold front moves in from the west today and slowly passes through by Thursday evening. The slow movement will allow for an extended period of rain (Our first since the remnants of Isaias) beginning later today. Most of the rain will fall overnight (there maybe a few rumbles of thunder) and gradually end from southwest to northeast by Thursday afternoon. Temperatures are quite mild ahead of the front.

Strong wind gusts are likely on the ridge tops today and tonight. The valleys have a decent southeasterly breeze but not the strong wind gusts up on the ridges.

The cold front stalls over central NC Friday. As of now, it looks like most of the rain will develop east of the High Country although, we can't completely rule out a brief shower or two.

Temperatures are above average once again Friday but much cooler air moves in Friday night and Saturday. Saturday is dry but chilly and breezy.

High pressure settles in Saturday through Tuesday. It will be dry with plenty of sunshine so the afternoons will be nice but mornings will be cold with hard freezes each morning Sunday through Tuesday.
